{{Short description|Spanish physicist}}
'''Rafael Armenteros''' (1922 – 5 March 2004) was a Spanish [[particle physics|particle physicist]], who was one of the leading figures in [[CERN]]'s various [[bubble chamber]] experiments.<ref>[http://cdsweb.cern.ch/record/726447 Obituary on CERN Document Server]</ref> Armenteros got his physics degree from [[Imperial College London]] in 1946,<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.imperial.ac.uk/centenary/memories/Richardson.shtml | title = Imperial College - Centenary website - Memories: Colleen Shilstone Richardson | access-date=22 April 2021 | year= 2007 }}</ref> and began his scientific career at the [[University of Manchester]]. After working on cosmic rays with [[Patrick Blackett|Blackett]] and [[Clifford Charles Butler|Butler]],<ref>{{cite journal | journal=Nature | year = 1951 | volume = 167 | pages = 501–503 | title = Decay of V-Particles | author = Armenteros, R. | issue = 4248 | display-authors=etal | doi = 10.1038/167501a0| pmid = 14826802 | bibcode = 1951Natur.167..501A }}</ref> and later with [[Louis Leprince-Ringuet | Leprince-Ringuet]] at [[École Polytechnique]],<ref>{{cite journal | author = Armenteros, R. | display-authors=etal | title = τ-Meson in the momentum cloud chamber of the école polytechnique | journal = Nuovo Cim | volume = 4 | pages = 217–220 | year = 1956 | issue=S2 | doi = 10.1007/BF02747880| bibcode=1956NCim....4S.217A }}</ref> he subsequently worked at CERN with Charles Peyrou.

Armenteros is best known for the method he co-devised with [[Jiří Podolský]] in 1953–1954.<ref>{{cite journal | title = III. Analysis of V-events | author1= J. Podolansky | author2= R. Armenteros | journal = The London, Edinburgh, and Dublin Philosophical Magazine and Journal of Science | volume= 45 | pages=13–30 | doi = 10.1080/14786440108520416 | year=1954| issue= 13 }}</ref> This technique is used in the analysis of the dynamics of two-body V decays and the relevant representation of data is known as an Armenteros-Podolansky plot.<ref>[http://www.phys.sinica.edu.tw/~spring8/presentation_files/TPCmeeting/20040820/TPC_0820.ppt A presentation by J.-L. Tang, giving the summary of the technique]</ref> These plots were among the first few public results from the [[LHC]] experiments, since {{Subatomic particle|link=yes|K-short0}} and (anti-)[[Lambda baryon|lambda]] particles studied this way provide good examples for the demonstration of the performance of the tracking systems.<ref>[https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/AtlasPublic/InDetTrackingPerformanceApprovedPlots#Run_1_2009_Collision_data Example plot] from the [[ATLAS experiment]].</ref>
